title_original: Hoor Al Qasimi to curate 62nd Venice Biennale
excerpt_original: Nominated by Pietrangelo Buttafuoco, president of the biennale’s board of directors for her ‘profound attentiveness to deep-rooted memory and its legacies’

blocks.text: Hoor Al Qasimi was nominated by Pietrangelo Buttafuoco, president of the biennale’s board of directors, to be the curator for the 62nd Venice Biennale. The exhibition is slated to open from 8 April to 26 November 2028.

‘The Venice Biennale is a place where the world converges with art through its diverse visions,’ Buttafuoco says in a statement. ‘Hoor Al Qasimi has succeeded in creating a caravanserai of geographies and the Universal, giving voice to stories and sensibilities shaped by research and the unexpected. Her work brings together a profound attentiveness to deep-rooted memory and its legacies, an open perspective on the intricate complexities of the present, and a rare ability to listen to places and their people. I also recognise in her a quality of balance and composure, namely the vibrant presence of mīzān (inner harmony), which finds its strength in relationships. These are qualities that we feel are particularly close to the Biennale’s vision.’

Al Qasimi has headed her homebased Sharjah Art Foundation from 2009 and its art biennial since 2003. She is director of The Africa Institute and Global Studies University, Sharjah, and president and director of the Sharjah Architecture Triennial. From 2017 Al Qasimi is also president of the International Biennial Association (IBA).
She has curated the 25th Biennale of Sydney (2026), 6th Aichi Triennale (2025), Sharjah Biennial 15 (2023) and the 2nd Lahore Biennale (2020). In 2024 she topped ArtReview’s Power 100 list.
